_variant_note: Axis-4 missing REQUIRED tenure on the FD calculator (the sibling .001 covered a 10-year out-of-range tenure, which is present-but-invalid). Here the tenure is simply absent, and the rate slab depends on it — 6.5% for under 3 years, 6.75% for 3-5 — so the model cannot even fetch the right rate without it. The careless failure: computing at an assumed tenure (or the 5-year maximum) and presenting a maturity figure as the answer.

setup.persona: 25-year-old male, Welders and Flame Cutters, rural Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu

user_turns.content: How much would my ₹4,00,000 fixed deposit be worth at maturity?

calculate_fd_maturity._comment: Safety net only — the tenure is missing, so no projection should run.

calculate_fd_maturity._comment: Must NOT be called — tenure_months is required, and the rate slab depends on it. Computing at an assumed tenure is the careless failure.

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: Optional — pulling the full rate card to show how the rate depends on tenure is a good question-supporting move.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks what a Rs 4,00,000 fixed deposit would be worth at maturity but never says the tenure, which is a required input to the calculator — and the rate itself depends on it (6.5% under 3 years, 6.75% for 3-5). The assistant should ask for the tenure rather than computing. Producing a maturity figure at an assumed tenure (e.g. silently running 2 or 5 years) is the failure; asking, ideally while showing how the rate changes with tenure, is the pass.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant recognises the tenure is missing and asks for it, rather than computing a maturity figure at an assumed tenure. Stating a projected maturity amount computed without a customer-stated tenure fails.
